releases.title: Runtime Intelligence and a better API workspace
releases.summary: FlexDoc can compare OpenAPI with routes registered by supported running frameworks. Try It and the API Client also share the same editor and scripting experience.
highlights: Runtime Intelligence shows matched, runtime-only and documented-only routes on supported backends.
Try It and the API Client share request editing, handoff state, command navigation and CodeMirror scripts.
Accessibility, responsive layouts and saved workspace preferences were tightened across the renderer.
Bundle size, large-spec rendering, caching, startup cost and memory use are measured in CI.

releases.title: Performance and production hardening
releases.summary: Added caching, ETags and repeatable performance checks for hosted documentation.
highlights: Node hosts cache generated docs pages and combine concurrent cold requests into one render.
Docs HTML supports deterministic ETag/304 revalidation while versioned renderer assets use long-lived caching.
CI tracks bundle size, large-spec rendering, startup time and memory use.
Static export remains available when you want no FlexDoc runtime work in the application.

releases.title: More REST body types and API-host execution
releases.summary: Added structured request bodies and server-side execution for requests that browser fetch cannot send.
highlights: URL-encoded, multipart, GraphQL and binary bodies work across editing, runs, import, History and replay.
Digest, Hawk, OAuth 1.0, AWS SigV4, NTLM intent and cookie API keys stay typed when imported or saved.
The Node backend can opt into cookie jars, configured mTLS certificates, Digest, Hawk, OAuth 1.0 and AWS SigV4.
Browser and host execution use the same response viewer, scripts, tests, History and collection runner.

releases.title: Collection runs, scripting help and History
releases.summary: Saved requests became repeatable workflows instead of isolated one-off calls.
highlights: Run collections and folders in saved order with progress, Stop and stop-on-failure controls.
Script IntelliSense adds completions, signatures, docs, variable keys and assertion help.
History adds search, grouped runs, response details, tests, logs, replay and deletion.
Send and collection runs use the same request, auth, variable, script and test logic.

releases.title: Postman import
releases.summary: Postman collections and environments can be imported into normal FlexDoc workspace data.
highlights: Import Postman Collection v2.1 requests, folders, variables, common auth, supported bodies and compatible scripts.
Import Postman environments into FlexDoc environments and keep them after reload.
Unsupported auth, script or body behavior is reported as a warning instead of being guessed.
Viewer settings and renderer options were also brought into the coordinated 2.8 release.

releases.title: Try It handoff and OAuth
releases.summary: Try It and the standalone API Client began sharing the same editable request state.
highlights: OpenAPI Try It can hand the live request directly into the API Client.
Inherited auth stays consistent across the handoff and saved request hierarchy.
Browser OAuth support expands beyond manually pasted access tokens.

releases.title: Persisted tests and script logs
releases.summary: Test results and script output became part of saved request History.
highlights: Post-response test results are saved with History entries.
Captured script output remains available after reload.
History keeps the validation context produced by the scripting runtime.

releases.title: Inherited auth and scripting
releases.summary: Shared authentication and script state reduced repeated setup across related requests.
highlights: Collection, folder and request auth follow an explicit inheritance chain.
OpenAPI authorization state carries into the API Client handoff.
OAuth access tokens and collection-variable scripting become reusable workspace features.

releases.title: Collection variables and nested folders
releases.summary: Collections gained the structure needed for larger reusable workspaces.
highlights: Collections can define reusable variables.
Folders can nest to arbitrary depth.
History replay keeps the request tied to its original collection.

releases.title: More backend frameworks
releases.summary: FlexDoc became available through native packages across the main backend ecosystems.
highlights: JavaScript/TypeScript hosts and native adapters use the same renderer contract.
.NET, JVM/Spring/JAX-RS, Python, PHP, Ruby, Go, Rust and Elixir gained native packaging or integrations.
Adapters serve local version-matched renderer assets instead of maintaining separate UI implementations.

releases.title: CLI, compatibility tests and API Client groundwork
releases.summary: The release added better validation, static docs tooling and the first pieces of the standalone API Client.
highlights: An OpenAPI compatibility corpus and browser regression tests define supported behavior.
The CLI can serve local docs and build self-contained static output.
Standalone API Client groundwork and Try It handoff started the broader workspace direction.
Prauga package migration and fingerprinted renderer assets made distribution more predictable.

releases.title: Module type resolution fixes
releases.summary: Fixed ESM/CommonJS type resolution so both module systems receive the right declarations.
highlights: Correct TypeScript declarations are selected for both ESM and CommonJS consumers.

releases.title: TypeScript package export fix
releases.summary: Fixed published client package type exports for TypeScript consumers.
highlights: Published client type declarations resolve correctly for TypeScript projects.

releases.title: Shared renderer architecture
releases.summary: FlexDoc moved to one renderer and one OpenAPI/request model shared across frontend and backend integrations.
highlights: One browser renderer handles navigation, schemas, Try It, code samples and theming.
OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 parsing and request serialization moved into shared core logic.
Backend packages became thin hosts for the shared renderer instead of separate documentation products.
